title: Hashcash Proof-of-Work
description: Secures chains with hashcash-style proof-of-work: find a nonce making the block hash meet the target. Work is verifiable instantly but expensive to produce; the longest-work chain wins. Bitcoin proved it at planetary scale.
key_mechanisms: Hash the block header with nonces

demo.title: Demo — Hashcash Proof-of-Work

title: Ethash Memory-Hard PoW
description: Uses memory-hard Ethash so commodity GPUs compete fairly with ASICs. The DAG forces memory bandwidth to matter; verification stays light. It was Ethereum's ASIC-resistance answer.

demo.title: Demo — Ethash Memory-Hard PoW

title: Casper Proof-of-Stake
description: Finalizes blocks with Casper-style proof-of-stake voting by bonded validators. Validators vote with their stake; finality comes in epochs, not probabilistic confirmations. Ethereum's merge made it the biggest PoS system.

demo.title: Demo — Casper Proof-of-Stake

title: Ouroboros PoS
description: Elects slot leaders with Ouroboros's provably-secure proof-of-stake. Stake-weighted lotteries pick leaders per slot; the protocol has peer-reviewed security proofs. Cardano runs it in production.

demo.title: Demo — Ouroboros PoS

title: Finality Gadgets
description: Adds finality gadgets that checkpoint the chain with validator supermajorities. Once finalized, history cannot reorganize without slashing a third of stake. It gives users irreversible confirmations.

demo.title: Demo — Finality Gadgets

title: Sync Committees
description: Uses rotating sync committees so light clients verify with small signatures. A few hundred validators sign each period; light clients track the committee, not the chain. It makes trust-minimized light clients practical.

demo.title: Demo — Sync Committees

title: Light Client Protocols
description: Syncs light clients with headers and proofs instead of full history. SPV-style verification checks proof-of-work or committee signatures on headers. Phones can verify without trusting servers.

demo.title: Demo — Light Client Protocols

title: Difficulty Adjustment
description: Retargets mining difficulty to keep block times constant as hash rate changes. Bitcoin adjusts every 2016 blocks; the formula compares actual versus target times. It is the protocol's thermostat.

demo.title: Demo — Difficulty Adjustment

title: Slashing Conditions
description: Slashes validators that equivocate or go offline, making attacks expensive. Provable misbehavior burns stake automatically; the economics deter rational attackers. It is PoS's security engine.

demo.title: Demo — Slashing Conditions

title: Validator Rotation
description: Rotates validator sets per epoch for decentralization and liveness. Entry and exit queues bound churn; rotation keeps any cabal from entrenching. It balances stability with openness.

demo.title: Demo — Validator Rotation

title: Checkpoint Sync
description: Syncs new nodes from recent finalized checkpoints instead of genesis. Weeks of history download in minutes; the checkpoint's finality is trusted via social consensus or embedded hashes. It is how nodes join fast.

demo.title: Demo — Checkpoint Sync

title: Fork Choice Rules
description: Chooses between competing chains with fork-choice rules like GHOST and LMD-GHOST. Most accumulated work — or most attested weight — decides; the rule keeps the network converged. It is the heart of consensus.

demo.title: Demo — Fork Choice Rules

title: Randomness Beacons
description: Generates unbiased randomness with beacons like RANDAO for leader election. Validators commit and reveal; the XOR is unpredictable and unbiasable enough. Fair lotteries need fair randomness.

demo.title: Demo — Randomness Beacons

title: Stake Delegation
description: Lets token holders delegate stake to validators without giving up custody. Delegators share rewards; validators gain weight. It decentralizes validation to small holders.

demo.title: Demo — Stake Delegation

title: Long-Range Attack Defense
description: Defends against long-range attacks where old keys rewrite history from afar. Weak subjectivity checkpoints bound how far back an attacker can fork; clients refuse ancient rewrites. It is PoS's answer to costless history.

demo.title: Demo — Long-Range Attack Defense
